rfi.title: Culture or Kremlin influence? Europe divided over its Russian Houses
rfi.description: A dispute between Germany and Russia over their cultural centres is drawing fresh attention to a network of Russian Houses that has faced years of accusations of propaganda and espionage, but continues to operate in several European countries.

rfi.title: British, French leaders hold talks on migrants and EU relations
rfi.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron held their first official talks on Thursday, with migrant boats, Ukraine and British-EU relations high on the agenda.

rfi.title: Former RFI journalist disappears in Niger after attempted coup
rfi.description: Reporters Without Borders has called for an investigation into the disappearance of Moussa Kaka, the director of a television station in Niger and a former correspondent for Radio France International, days after a failed coup in the country.

rfi.title: France asserts sovereignty over disputed Pacific islands as Vanuatu turns to ICJ
rfi.description: France has insisted on its sovereignty over two Pacific islands claimed by Vanuatu, which has opened a case at the International Court of Justice.

rfi.title: EU lawmakers demand Brussels force Meta to 'protect' European children
rfi.description: European Union lawmakers have demanded that the bloc's executive compel Meta to change the "addictive" design of its platforms in Europe, as the giant has promised to do in some US states, according to a letter seen by the French news agency AFP on Thursday.

rfi.title: Three Pacific hurricanes gather strength as El Nino intensifies
rfi.description: The current El Nino could become the strongest on record as the natural climate pattern that warms the tropical Pacific intensifies, with three hurricanes churning across the ocean on Thursday. The United Nations has warned of growing extreme weather risks into 2027.

rfi.title: Ebola deaths in DR Congo top 3,000 as WHO says vaccine trials imminent
rfi.description: More than 3,000 people have died of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the latest figures show, as the World Health Organisation says trials of three potential vaccines against the strain behind the current outbreak should begin within weeks.

rfi.title: Nepal seeks climate justice after Himalayan disaster
rfi.description: When a wall of icy debris from a glacial collapse on the China-Nepal border tore through his village last week, Pemba Chhring Tamang watched the landscape he had known all his life disappear.

rfi.title: EU suspends Brazilian meat imports over antibiotic concerns
rfi.description: The European Union has suspended imports of Brazilian meat and other animal products, as Brussels waits for assurances that the South American country is complying with the bloc’s rules on antibiotic use in livestock farming.

rfi.title: French filmmakers and local fixer freed after weeks in Togo detention
rfi.description: Two French documentary makers and their Togolese fixer have been granted provisional release in Togo, more than a month after they were arrested in the north while working on a television programme. The three deny accusations of false statements and irregularities linked to their filming assignment.

rfi.title: EU summons Russian envoy, eyes sanctions after Germany drone 'attack'
rfi.description: The European Union summoned Russia's top diplomat and signaled it may impose new sanctions on Wednesday, after last month's drone incident in Germany that the bloc's foreign policy chief branded "state-sponsored terrorism."

rfi.title: World set to breach 1.5C climate limit as UN urges rapid reversal
rfi.description: Global warming is set to cross the 1.5C limit within the next few years, exposing people and ecosystems to more severe climate damage, the UN's environmental agency said on Wednesday. But temperatures could eventually be brought back down if emissions fall sharply and carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere.

rfi.title: Senegal and IMF strike $2.2bn deal, two years after debt scandal froze funding
rfi.description: Senegal and the International Monetary Fund have reached a staff-level agreement on a new $2.2 billion (€1.9 billion) lending programme, nearly two years after an earlier deal was suspended following the discovery of previously unreported public debt.

rfi.title: French pop star Patrick Bruel cancels 35-date tour amid sexual assault storm
rfi.description: French pop and variety singer Patrick Bruel has cancelled his entire 35-date autumn tour, bowing to weeks of pressure from politicians, mayors and feminist groups following allegations of sexual assault and rape against him. Lawyers representing the accusers called the decision a "power signal" showing that women are "at last being heard."

rfi.title: Tunisia accused of shutting down civil society through sweeping crackdown
rfi.description: Tunisian authorities have intensified pressure on civil society through arrests, prosecutions, financial investigations and mass suspensions, Human Rights Watch said on Wednesday – warning that the independent civic space created after the 2011 revolution has been all but shut down.

rfi.title: Clooney kicks off Venice as festival wades into war, Gaza and AI
rfi.description: Venice rolls out the red carpet Wednesday, with George Clooney set to collect a lifetime achievement award as the film festival opens a starry two-week run heavy on biopics, war-zone dramas from Gaza and Iran, and a fresh reckoning with artificial intelligence.

rfi.title: Nepal glacier disaster toll passes 1,000 as calls for climate justice grow
rfi.description: The death toll from last week's devastating Himalayan glacial floods passed 1,000 on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors. Nepal's foreign minister said the disaster was "a warning signal" of the growing risks posed by climate change.

rfi.title: DRC school year begins amid Ebola, strikes and conflict
rfi.description: Millions of students returned to school across the Democratic Republic of Congo on Tuesday, but the new term began amid an Ebola outbreak affecting six provinces, a teachers’ strike call and continuing conflict in the east. In AFC/M23-controlled territories, the movement organised the return to classrooms even as Kinshasa continued to pay primary and secondary school teachers.

lemonde.title: Radio France : pour Sibyle Veil, « c’est la grandeur du service public que d’être pluraliste »
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », la présidente-directrice générale de Radio France confirme, malgré la menace de grève, maintenir le recrutement d’un journaliste de « Valeurs actuelles » à l’éditorial politique du dimanche sur France Inter. Elle répond aussi, pour la première fois, à Thomas Legrand qui l’accuse d’avoir cédé aux pressions de l’extrême droite.

lemonde.title: L’été 2026 devient, de très loin, le plus chaud jamais enregistré : « Battre le record de presque 1 °C sur une saison, c’est énorme »
lemonde.description: Une telle saison estivale, qui avait une chance sur cent de se produire aujourd’hui, aurait été quasiment impossible sans réchauffement climatique d’origine humaine.

lemonde.title: Après les inondations dans l’Himalaya, la Chine impose un contrôle strict des informations liées au Tibet
lemonde.description: Depuis la catastrophe du 26 août, la couverture de l’actualité de la région, hautement sensible pour les autorités, est réduite aux informations données par Pékin, qui fait la part belle aux opérations de secours. Le pouvoir censure les contenus publiés par les citoyens et bannit l’accès à la zone meurtrie pour les journalistes étrangers.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Donald Trump veut réclamer à l’Europe le remboursement de l’aide américaine à Kiev
lemonde.description: Dans un message particulièrement virulent, le président américain a reproché jeudi à son prédécesseur, Joe Biden, d’avoir fourni gratuitement à l’Ukraine des centaines de milliards de dollars d’aide et de munitions, estimant que les Européens auraient dû en assumer le coût.

lemonde.title: A Lyon, agressions racistes et affrontements entre supporteurs rivaux autour du stade de l’OL
lemonde.description: Une élue agressée, son compagnon blessé, un adolescent hospitalisé. La violence à connotation raciste marque le début de saison du club lyonnais. Les autorités évoquent des affrontements entre supporteurs, qui pourraient être le point de départ de ce climat de violence.

lemonde.title: Chidimma Adetshina, la Miss dont l’Afrique du Sud, en pleine vague xénophobe, ne veut pas
lemonde.description: La jeune femme de 25 ans est au cœur d’un feuilleton migratoire et judiciaire avec les autorités sud-africaines depuis 2024, après sa participation avortée au concours de Miss Afrique du Sud. Elle avait quitté la compétition après avoir été victime d’une vague de haine, remettant en cause sa citoyenneté.

lemonde.title: Le conseil de surveillance de Volkswagen approuve un plan de restructuration prévoyant la suppression de 50 000 postes
lemonde.description: Le constructeur allemand estime qu’une « adaptation conséquente des capacités de personnel à la réalité économique est indispensable », en raison de la pression concurrentielle mondiale croissante, des mutations de la demande et de la technologie.

lemonde.title: Au procès de Bertrand Venteau, le président de la Coordination rurale, deux mondes qui s’opposent
lemonde.description: Devant le tribunal correctionnel d’Auch, jeudi 3 septembre, le syndicaliste agricole a reconnu et assumé les propos qu’il avait tenus le 19 décembre 2025, quand il disait vouloir « faire la peau aux écolos ».

lemonde.title: L’économie allemande amorce sa reprise, portée par les exportations vers l’Europe et l’IA
lemonde.description: Deux instituts de conjoncture ont nettement relevé leurs prévisions de croissance pour 2026, avec des signes de reprise bien plus favorables que prévu.

lemonde.title: Crise de Ceuta : Pedro Sanchez continue d’écarter la responsabilité du Maroc, mais nuance sa position
lemonde.description: Devant le Parlement, le président du gouvernement espagnol a défendu la gestion de l’afflux massif de migrants, fin juillet, tout en reconnaissant des défaillances du côté marocain de la frontière. Il demandera un renforcement de la présence européenne dans l’enclave.

lemonde.title: Itamar Ben Gvir, ministre israélien suprémaciste, présente un plan pour vider la bande de Gaza de ses habitants, durant la campagne des élections législatives
lemonde.description: Mercredi, le ministre de la défense, Israël Katz, a aussi assuré que l’Etat hébreu était prêt à transférer les Palestiniens hors de Gaza, à condition que les Etats-Unis donnent leur accord. Le déplacement forcé d’une population civile est un crime de guerre, au regard du droit international.

lemonde.title: Mayotte : les méthodes contestées de la police pour intercepter les migrants en mer
lemonde.description: Un dossier judiciaire auquel « Le Monde » a eu accès illustre les pratiques parfois dangereuses des autorités. En 2019, un jeune migrant a perdu ses deux jambes, déchiquetées par les hélices d’un bateau lors d’une interception des forces de l’ordre.

lemonde.title: Gabriel Attal dévoile une équipe de campagne présidentielle sans poids lourds politiques mais avec de « nouveaux visages »
lemonde.description: Sans cesse ramené à Emmanuel Macron et à son duel avec Edouard Philippe pour l’élection présidentielle 2027, le candidat prône le « renouvellement » et a notamment choisi l’ancienne judoka et journaliste Céline Géraud pour piloter sa communication.

lemonde.title: Fondée par des Français, la start-up d’intelligence artificielle Hugging Face défend son rachat par l’américain Nvidia, au nom de l’« open source »
lemonde.description: La plateforme de référence pour la publication de modèles d’IA ouverts vient d’être rachetée pour 13 milliards de dollars par le géant mondial des processeurs. Une acquisition qui illustre la difficulté en Europe de conserver ses champions technologiques.

lemonde.title: Au Yémen, les combats entre forces gouvernementales et rebelles houthistes s’intensifient
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement yéménite avait averti, le mois dernier, que les rebelles cherchaient à prendre position aux abords du détroit de Bab Al-Mandab. Selon une source militaire, les combats les plus intenses ont lieu entre la ville portuaire de Moka, sur la côte ouest, et Taëz.

lemonde.title: Nouvelle-Calédonie : l’Etat accorde une aide financière et relance le débat institutionnel
lemonde.description: Venue à Paris pour alerter sur les risques de banqueroute qui menace la collectivité, la délégation transpartisane calédonienne a obtenu des subventions supplémentaires, outre les 430 millions prévus en 2026 dans le pacte de refondation. Un soutien conditionné à la poursuite des réformes économiques.

euronews.title: Berlin airport terminal evacuated after hazardous materials alert
euronews.description: A woman reports carrying toxic substances in her handbag at Berlin airport. Police arrest her and evacuate Terminal 1.

euronews.description: The US recognises Britain's administration of the Falkland Islands but remains neutral over the competing sovereignty claims.

euronews.title: 'Highly likely' Russia will escalate attacks on EU, Lithuanian minister says
euronews.description: While commending Berlin for attributing the attempted Leipzig drone attack to Russia, Lithuania's foreign affairs minister warns stronger EU-wide deterrence is needed to prevent further escalation.

euronews.title: France had its hottest summer since records began over a century ago, environment minister says
euronews.description: According to Meteo France, the summer of 2026 recorded an average temperature of 24 °C covering day and nighttime, 3.6 C above the normal average, and higher than in 2003, when temperatures were 2.7 C above normal.

euronews.title: Lisbon: MOTELX launches 20th edition with expanded programme and plenty of horror
euronews.description: Marking its 20th edition, the festival stretches over more days and more venues, packed with new discoveries and cult favourites at Portugal's scariest film event.

euronews.title: Former French President Hollande publishes new book with plan for France, but remains undecided about running
euronews.description: Former French President Hollande published his newest book on Thursday, laying out 80 policy proposals. Despite his book somewhat resembling a manifesto, the former president maintains he will wait until December to decide whether to run.

euronews.title: 'Anti-fast-fashion' law: France rejects China's discrimination claims
euronews.description: China has claimed that the new "anti-fast-fashion" law which came into force in France on Tuesday amounts to "discrimination." Responding to these accusations, a source from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs told Euronews that such claims were false.

euronews.title: Two arrested after attack on defence companies in Munich
euronews.description: In Munich, a man and a woman allegedly attempted to carry out an arson attack outside the premises of two defence companies. The pair were arrested.

euronews.title: Russians skewer authorities for ordering citizens to register their chicken
euronews.description: A government decree requiring registration of domestic birds, camels and reindeer took effect Tuesday, sending Russians to government service centres with live chickens in tow before authorities clarified that owners did not need to bring their animals anywhere.

euronews.title: Iranian café chain mogul jailed and stripped of assets for backing January protests
euronews.description: Sadegh Saeedinia, manager of the Saeedinia café chain, was convicted of "propaganda against national security" for posting about the January protests on Instagram and encouraging staff to strike, in one of the harshest sentences handed to a private entrepreneur since the unrest.

euronews.title: France tests Tesla self-driving two months after calling it too risky
euronews.description: After a "constructive exchange" on Wednesday evening between Elon Musk and Philippe Tabarot, the transport minister hailed "a new step" in authorising this type of vehicle.

euronews.title: Thousands of Ukrainian children still at risk in Russia as EU prepares new sanctions
euronews.description: Thousands of Ukrainian children remain under Russian control, facing indoctrination, militarisation and the loss of their identity, the Bring Kids Back UA initiative warned as the EU prepares new sanctions against those responsible for their deportation.

euronews.title: How public-private partnerships are driving new investment
euronews.description: Public-private partnerships are opening new opportunities for investment and development, from renewable energy and digital infrastructure to water and desalination. The episode looks at how cooperation between government and business could shape Azerbaijan’s next phase of growth.

euronews.title: EU suspension of Brazilian meat comes into force, despite ongoing talks with Brasília
euronews.description: Brazil has yet to provide the necessary guarantees to allow an audit of its beef exports’ compliance with EU food safety standards, while inspections of poultry and honey imports are already under way.

euronews.title: Macron and Burnham hail stronger UK-France ties at Downing Street talks
euronews.description: Burnham and his wife, Marie-France van Heel, welcomed the French president and First Lady Brigitte Macron outside the famous black door of 10 Downing Street.

euronews.title: General charged over Kyiv children's hospital strike shot in Russia
euronews.description: Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich, commander of a heavy bomber division and charged in absentia by Ukraine over the 2024 Okhmatdyt children's hospital strike, was shot twice by a motorbike gunman near Engels airbase and airlifted to Moscow in serious condition.

euronews.title: Chilean penguins fitted with vests to protect healing wounds
euronews.description: Injured Humboldt penguins in Chile are fitted with recovery vests designed to protect wounds and prevent them from damaging stitches as they heal.

euronews.title: New school year: Which EU countries pay their teachers the most?
euronews.description: It's back-to-school time again, and teachers and their unions are reigniting the debate over stagnant wages and recurring staff shortages. But which countries pay teachers the best?

zeit.description: Das BSW verliert in Thüringen drei Abgeordnete. Parteigründerin Sarah Wagenknecht wertet die Aktion als Versuch, dem Bündnis vor anstehenden Landtagswahlen zu schaden.

zeit.description: Der VW-Aufsichtsrat hat den umstrittenen Sanierungsplan des Vorstands angenommen. Für vier Werke kann demnach keine Folgebelegung bis 2034 gewährleistet werden.

zeit.title: Gazastreifen: Rechtsextremer Ben Gvir will Palästinenser in wenigen Jahren umsiedeln
zeit.description: Israels Sicherheitsminister Ben Gvir will eine Umsiedlung von Bewohnern des Gazastreifens vorantreiben. Er plant die Ausreise von zwei Millionen Menschen.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : la Cour de cassation confirme les lourdes peines dans l’affaire du "complot contre l’État"
france24fr.description: La Cour de cassation tunisienne a rejeté jeudi le pourvoi dans l’affaire du "complot contre la sûreté de l’État", confirmant les lourdes peines prononcées en appel, en novembre 2025, contre une quarantaine de personnes, dont des figures de l’opposition et des avocats.

france24fr.title: Iran : les Etats-Unis ont-ils visé une cérémonie de mariage ?
france24fr.description: Dans leurs frappes récentes contre l'Iran, les Etats-Unis sont accusés d'avoir bombardé une cérémonie de mariage, dans la région du détroit d'Ormuz. Des images vérifiées tournées après l'attaque montrent les dégâts qu'elle a occasionnés et les décombres alentour. L'armée américaine a assuré ne pas viser de civils.

france24fr.title: Ambassade de France en Irak : les descendants de propriétaires juifs assignent l’État français
france24fr.description: Nouveau front judiciaire dans le litige autour de l’ambassade de France en Irak. Les descendants des propriétaires juifs du bâtiment ont assigné l’État français à Paris et réclament 21,5 millions d’euros, une somme correspondant selon eux aux loyers impayés depuis plus de cinquante ans et au préjudice moral subi.

france24fr.title: L'extrême droite en tête des élections régionales en Allemagne : le retour des vieux démons ?
france24fr.description: L’AfD, le parti d’extrême droite en Allemagne, est bien placé pour remporter la victoire dans le Land de Saxe-Anhalt dans l'Est du pays dimanche 6 septembre. Cela serait la première fois qu’un parti d’extrême droite prendrait le pouvoir depuis 1945. L’AfD est en tête dans les sondages avec près de 40% des intentions de vote. france24fr.title: Football : s'estimant "humilié" Aubameyang ne veut plus jouer avec le Gabon
france24fr.description: ⚽🇬🇦 Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang ne veut plus jouer avec le Gabon. Le capitaine des Panthères a annoncé sa mise en retrait de l’équipe nationale, s’estimant "humilié" après son exclusion puis sa réintégration à la suite de l’échec à la CAN 2025 au Maroc.

france24fr.title: "On n’aura plus d’automne ni d’hiver" : pourquoi l’épisode El Niño attendu fin 2026 inquiète
france24fr.description: L’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM) a annoncé jeudi que le phénomène climatique El Niño va se renforcer dans les prochains mois pour atteindre une intensité "très forte" d’ici la fin de l’année et se maintenir jusqu'en février 2027. Sécheresses, inondations, chaleurs extrêmes : décryptage d’un phénomène naturel dont les effets sont amplifiés par le réchauffement climatique.

france24fr.title: À Kiev, l’étrange guerre des espions ukrainiens en plein conflit avec la Russie
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a rappelé à l’ordre, mercredi, les deux principaux services de renseignement du pays dont les membres se sont tirés dessus. Un incident qui révèle la rivalité entre les espions ukrainiens.

france24fr.title: Italie : le combat d'une famille pour scolariser leur enfant
france24fr.description: Au large de la Sicile, sur l'île de Stromboli, le plus petite école d'Europe rouvre ses portes pour une seule élève, Aïsha.

france24fr.title: Agriculture : une serre adaptée aux futures canicules
france24fr.description: Le changement climatique pousse à adapter les manières de cultiver. Ces serres spéciales pourrait être une partie de la solution. Elle permettent de continuer à faire pousser fruits et légumes malgré des épisodes caniculaires intenses

france24fr.title: Pourquoi ces jeunes des quartiers partent gravir un sommet dans les Alpes ?
france24fr.description: Et si la montagne pouvait rapprocher les jeunes des quartiers populaires de ceux qui n’y vivent pas ? À Nantes, quatre jeunes se lancent dans une aventure hors du commun : une semaine d’alpinisme dans les Alpes, accompagnés de mentors issus du monde professionnel.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : une nouvelle étape franchie dans la lutte contre la drépanocytose
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, un médicament générique fabriqué sur place redonne espoir aux malades de drépanocytose. Une avancée qui permet de réduire la dépendance du continent vis à vis des médicaments importés d'Europe et des États-Unis.

france24fr.title: Iran : "leur monnaie ne vaut plus rien" se félicite Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Suite aux frappes américaines menées contre l'Iran, le pays est en pleine récession économique. Les commerçants n'ont parfois pas d'autre choix que de fermer leur magasin alors que les autorités iraniennes tentent de maintenir, comme elles le peuvent, l'économie du pays.

france24fr.title: France : 230 kg de cocaïne découverts dans une climatisation près de Dijon
france24fr.description: Les douaniers ont annoncé ce 2 septembre avoir saisi 231 kilos de cocaïne, pour une valeur estimée à 6,8 millions d'euros, sur l'autoroute entre Beaune et Dijon, dans un poids lourd immatriculé aux Pays-Bas venant d'Espagne.

france24fr.title: Réchauffement climatique : les Palaos, îles du Pacifique, en première ligne
france24fr.description: Les Palaos s'inquiètent face au changement climatique. Trois cyclones ont, en même temps, balayé le Pacifique à cause du phénomène El Niño, d'une intensité historique cette année. Selon un rapport de l'ONU, le défi n'est plus d'éviter le dépassement de 1,5 degré prévu par l'Accord de Paris il y a 11 ans, mais d'apprendre à le gérer.

france24fr.title: Le géant des puces Nvidia rachète Hugging Face, la pépite au cœur de l'IA "ouverte"
france24fr.description: Le patron de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, a annoncé jeudi que son entreprise allait débourser 12,9 milliards de dollars pour prendre le contrôle de Hugging Face, une plateforme franco-américaine qui propose des modèles d'IA ouverts accessibles gratuitement. Cette acquisition, la deuxième la plus importante de l'histoire de l'entreprise, illustre la volonté de diversification du géant des puces graphiques.

france24fr.title: Royaume-Uni : premier entretien Burnham-Macron pour "renforcer" les relations
france24fr.description: Le nouveau Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham et le président français Emmanuel Macron ont affiché aujourd'hui à Londres leur volonté de "renforcer" les relations entre le Royaume-Uni et la France mais aussi l'Union européenne, au lendemain d'une première rencontre autour de la tapisserie de Bayeux.

france24fr.title: "Notre vie a changé" : deux mois après le double séisme, un Vénézuélien témoigne
france24fr.description: Un double séisme a frappé le nord du Venezuela le 24 juin, faisant plus de 6 500 morts. Environ deux mois après, un habitant de Catia La Mar, l’une des villes touchées, raconte comment la vie quotidienne a été bouleversée par la catastrophe.

spiegel.description: Weitere 50.000 Jobs sollen wegfallen, vier Werke stehen auf der Kippe: Der Aufsichtsrat hat den VW-​Sanierungsplan gebilligt.

spiegel.title: Spahn wird Mitglied des Haushaltsausschusses
spiegel.description: Die politische Karriere von Jens Spahn geht weiter. Erst Mitte Juli war er nach scharfer Kritik als Fraktionschef der Union zurückgetreten. Nun zieht er in einen der einflussreichsten Ausschüsse des Bundestages ein.

spiegel.title: Hape Kerkeling warnt vor »Kapitulation der Fakten vor der Lautstärke«
spiegel.description: Entertainer Hape Kerkeling hat die SPD-Abgeordneten an den Mut ihres ehemaligen Parteivorsitzenden Otto Wels erinnert. Und sie aufgefordert: Das Land dürfe Verfassungsfeinden und deren Gegnern nicht denselben Raum lassen.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt - News zur Landtagswahl: Didi Hallervorden nennt Schulze den »richtigen Mann« für Sachsen-Anhalt
spiegel.description: Kabarettist Dieter Hallervorden ruft in Halle dazu auf, gegen die AfD zu stimmen. Den Kanzler kritisiert er trotzdem. Und: Ein Viertel der Wähler ist laut ZDF-Politbarometer kurz vor dem Urnengang noch unentschlossen. Das News-Update.

spiegel.title: CDU in Sachsen-Anhalt: Drei Tage vor der Wahl eskaliert der Streit
spiegel.description: Die CDU in Sachsen-Anhalt taumelt der Wahl entgegen. Der Kanzler wird im Wahlkampf versteckt. Die Umfragen sind schlecht. Jetzt kommt noch ein offener Zwist über den Umgang mit der Linken dazu.

spiegel.title: Brandenburg: Polizei prüft Bekennerschreiben zu Angriff auf Stromnetz
spiegel.description: Zu dem Angriff auf die Stromversorgungsanlage in Jänschwalde ist ein Bekennerschreiben aufgetaucht. Die Polizei prüft auch Hinweise aus der Bevölkerung. Brandenburg will rasch Konsequenzen ziehen.

spiegel.title: Elektroauto: Ehrliche Klimarechnung als Lüge
spiegel.description: Ein Diskussionspapier der TU München zur Klimabilanz von Elektroautos hat für Wirbel gesorgt. Der Vorschlag der Professoren, nicht nur auf die fehlenden Abgase zu schauen, kann sinnvoll sein. Doch wem nützt er wirklich?

spiegel.title: »Schwarze Samstage« von Maxim Biller: Selbsterforschung des Besserwissers
spiegel.description: Maxim Biller wollte keine Romane mehr schreiben. »Schwarze Samstage« ist auch keiner. Sondern eine überraschend ehrliche Bestandsaufnahme angesichts der Folgen des Terrorüberfalls des 7. Oktober.

spiegel.title: Kritische Infrastruktur: Verfassungsschutz warnt vor Spionage und Sabotage
spiegel.description: Die beiden jüngsten Anschläge auf das deutsche Stromnetz zeigen die Verwundbarkeit des Energiesektors. Nur wenige Tage vor den Taten hatten Verfassungsschützer Unternehmen gewarnt. Mit deutlichen Worten.

spiegel.title: Ulrich Siegmund: Der Posterboy der AfD – SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Ulrich Siegmund gibt den nahbaren Kumpel, seine AfD führt die Umfragen in Sachsen-Anhalt an. Hinter den Kulissen indes wirken rechtsextreme Ideologen.

spiegel.title: Hockenheim: Alphaville will nach Wiedereinladung nicht mehr beim Glücksgefühle-Festival auftreten
spiegel.description: Die Ausladung der Band Alphaville vom Glücksgefühle-Festival hat für erhebliche Kritik gesorgt. Der Veranstalter räumt einen Fehler ein. Die Musiker haben nun trotzdem endgültig abgesagt.

spiegel.title: Gianni Infantino in der Kritk: Wer wird in einem Jahr Fifa-Präsident sein?
spiegel.description: Fifa‑Präsident Gianni Infantino steht nach der Aufregung über seinen Investorenplan massiv in der Kritik. Aber reicht das, um ihn abzulösen? Sportrechtler Martin Nolte erläutert den Machtkampf im Weltfußball.

spiegel.title: Filmfestspiele in Venedig: Werner Herzog erzählt von irischen Schwestern
spiegel.description: Immerhin, der Film ist von Altmeister Werner Herzog. Er zeigt die heitere Weltflucht zweier irischer Schwestern, die ihre Sätze stets gemeinsam sprechen. Eine Kampfansage an den banalen Einzelmenschenalltag. Und: richtig lustig.

spiegel.title: Tierschutz: »Auch Haustiere werden systematisch gequält«
spiegel.description: Madeleine Martin hat 34 Jahre lang dafür gekämpft, dass Tiere besser leben können. Dabei hat sie viel über Halter gelernt, die sich selbst belügen.

spiegel.title: Sabotage: Offenbar 165 Verdachtsfälle in Deutschland in diesem Jahr
spiegel.description: Es waren Attacken auf Stromleitungen und Bahntrassen, Angriffe mit Drohnen: Einem Medienbericht zufolge hat das BKA diese hybride Bedrohung für Deutschland in einem alarmierenden Lagebericht zusammengefasst.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: Diese Wählergruppen halten noch zum CDU-Kanzler
spiegel.description: Friedrich Merz ist als Kanzler historisch unbeliebt. Der Ipsos-Politikmonitor des SPIEGEL zeichnet den Absturz seit Amtsantritt nach. Und zeigt, welche Kabinettsmitglieder besser ankommen als ihr Chef.

observador.title: Do carro ao atrelado. Os processos em que Neves é alvo
observador.description: Procurador-geral da República esclareceu que Neves está a ser investigado em cinco casos, três deles inquéritos-crime. Os que envolvem o atrelado apreendido e as obras no Alentejo são "urgentes".

observador.title: 23h. Casos Mai. Ventura pede intervenção pública de Seguro
observador.description: Líder do Chega diz diz que o Presidente da República é um dos mais interessados em resolver as polémicas. Ainda nesta edição, Iniciativa Liberal vai votar contra a moção de censura do Chega.

observador.title: Afinal Ministério contradiz Neves sobre destruição de bidões
observador.description: Valor de 144 mil euros usado por Luís Neves para justificar a não destruição dos bidões incluía químicos de múltiplos processos, não só da Operação Pacoba.

observador.title: Ceuta. Moradores contra centro de detenção para migrantes
observador.description: Dois novos centros de acolhimento — um junto a uma creche, outro no Cais Oeste — concentram a revolta dos residentes, que ameaçam continuar os protestos até o Governo recuar.

observador.title: Greve nos bares dos comboios da CP mantém adesão de 95%
observador.description: Trabalhadores da Itau, concessionária dos bares dos comboios Alfa Pendular e Intercidades, exigem cumprimento do acordo de empresa e pedem intervenção do Governo.

observador.title: 980 euros: o reembolso médio de IRS em 2026
observador.description: Quase todos os 2.660 milhões a devolver já foram pagos. Número de declarações com reembolso subiu 3,5% e o montante cresceu 8,6% face à campanha anterior.

observador.title: Ministério espera fim da auditoria à PJ até fim do ano
observador.description: O gabinete de Rita Alarcão Júdice garante que a IGSJ entregará resultados até final de 2026. Amadeu Guerra confirmou três processos a envolver o ministro.

observador.title: Baerbock: ONU não sobrevive sem reformas
observador.description: Na última conferência de imprensa antes de ceder o cargo, Baerbock alertou para a burocracia excessiva e o impasse no Conselho de Segurança. Vai agora lecionar em Columbia.

observador.title: Bruxelas afasta risco imediato no abastecimento de gás
observador.description: Armazenamento na UE está nos 65,85%, com prazo até dezembro para atingir os 90% obrigatórios. Portugal destaca-se com 93,08% de reservas.

observador.title: Kristin. Leiria investe em geradores e comunicações
observador.description: Os SMAS de Leiria vão realizar um investimento de cerca de "250 mil euros" em geradores para garantir o abastecimento de água e as comunicações, após a tempestade Kristin no ano passado.

observador.title: Chapo: paz em Cabo Delgado é prioridade para as crianças
observador.description: No Parlamento Infantil, o Presidente moçambicano elegeu o fim do conflito em Cabo Delgado como prioridade máxima. Um milhão de crianças precisa de ajuda humanitária no país.

observador.title: 22h. Nepal. Nações Unidas aumentam pacote de apoio
observador.description: Pelo menos mil 280 pessoas morreram nas enxurradas que atingiram a região da fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete. Ainda, Iniciativa Liberal vai votar contra moção de censura ao Governo.

observador.title: Trump: munições "quase ilimitadas" para guerra com o Irão
observador.description: Seis meses depois do início do conflito, o Presidente norte-americano diz que os EUA acumulam produção recorde e retomam em breve vendas de armamento a aliados.

observador.title: Clássicos no Dragão já têm datas marcadas
observador.description: Na sétima e na 12.ª jornadas da I Liga, FC Porto receberá Benfica e Sporting, respetivamente. Ambos os jogos serão ao domingo às 20h30, no Estádio do Dragão.

observador.title: ONU funde duas agências de ensino numa só
observador.description: A Assembleia-Geral aprovou a fusão da UNSSC com o UNITAR no âmbito da reforma ONU80 de Guterres, que prevê cortes de 15% nas despesas e até 20% no pessoal.

observador.title: Nepal: ONU aumenta para 2,15 milhões a ajuda após cheias
observador.description: Inundações de 26 de agosto destruíram estradas e pontes numa faixa de 72 km. ONU e Governo nepalês preparam apelo humanitário de emergência de quatro meses.

observador.title: Putin garante que a Rússia tem condições para gerir o défice
observador.description: Putin confirmou que o défice do orçamento federal registou uma subida de 40% no primeiro semestre deste ano, fixando-se agora em cerca de 2,8% do Produto Interno Bruto do país.

observador.title: Zelensky espera enviados de Trump em Kiev "nos próximos dias
observador.description: Zelensky disse ter "datas preliminares" para reunir com Witkoff e Kushner, que já visitaram Moscovo várias vezes mas nunca Kiev desde o regresso de Trump.

elpais.title: Sánchez da un giro y avisa de que si encuentra pruebas contra Marruecos actuará
elpais.description: El presidente avanza un replanteamiento de la cooperación en la frontera pero se queda solo en su cautela: todo el Congreso cree que fue Marruecos

elpais.title: El Gobierno convocó a la embajadora de Marruecos por las “declaraciones inaceptables” sobre Ceuta y Melilla de dos ministros
elpais.description: Karima Benyaich, que estaba fuera de España en ese momento, no acudió a la cita; en su lugar asistió el encargado de negocios, según Exteriores

elpais.title: Ceuta, no hay más tiempo que perder
elpais.description: La solución a la crisis humanitaria y política exige la plena implicación del Estado y redefinir la relación con Marruecos

elpais.title: Feijóo acusa a Sánchez de estar “chantajeado” por Marruecos y le avisa: “Pagará ante la justicia”
elpais.description: El líder del PP se reafirma en culpar a Marruecos de la operación del salto masivo: “Hay indicios de que la coordinó”

elpais.title: Margarita Robles evita aplaudir el anuncio de Sánchez sobre la publicación de los informes sobre Ceuta
elpais.description: La ministra de Defensa, que ha mostrado diferencias con el resto del Gobierno acerca de la crisis en Ceuta, no ha seguido a la bancada socialista en la ovación tras el anuncio del presidente del Gobierno

elpais.title: Marlaska se queja ante el Poder Judicial de que la jueza pidiera a la Policía no informarle sobre Ceuta
elpais.description: La presidenta del CGPJ respalda a la instructora de la Audiencia Nacional y asegura que cumplió con su función: “Debemos mostrar el máximo respeto”

elpais.title: Muere un migrante en un centro de menores por complicaciones asociadas a la diabetes que padecía
elpais.description: El joven de 17 años estaba a cargo de la ciudad autónoma y  ha muerto por una hipoglucemia severa, según fuentes de Sanidad

elpais.title: Detenida una mujer ceutí por el homicidio de un migrante en situación irregular
elpais.description: El hombre se encontraba alojado en la casa de la presunta homicida

elpais.title: Milei acusa a Sánchez de facilitar la llegada de “hordas extranjeras” para destruir “la identidad española”
elpais.description: El presidente argentino usa la crisis de Ceuta para arremeter contra su par español desde el Foro Madrid en Chile

elpais.title: Calzoncillos enterrados para medir la salud del suelo y cucarachas ‘lecheras’: los Ig Nobel premian los estudios más insólitos del año
elpais.description: La ceremonia, en la que participan nobeles reales, se ha trasladado de la Universidad de Harvard a Suiza por las políticas de Trump

elpais.title: Uno de los miembros del jurado del caso Lindsay Clancy discrepa de los otros 11 y no hay veredicto, ¿qué pasa si el bloqueo continúa?
elpais.description: Por tercer día, el jurado se declara incapaz de llegar a la unanimidad, necesaria para que el juicio a la mujer que estranguló a sus tres hijos no sea declarado nulo

elpais.title: Los grandes ‘chatbots’ de inteligencia artificial sufren una caída global y dejan de funcionar
elpais.description: Los usuarios de las plataformas de ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Copilot y Gemini registran problemas desde hace unas horas

elpais.title: David Broncano: “Temo que esta sea mi última presentación en TVE, todos sabemos lo que puede pasar”
elpais.description: El humorista será uno de los protagonistas de la nueva temporada de la cadena pública, que avanzó sus grandes apuestas este miércoles en Prado del Rey

elpais.title: Marcos Llorente anuncia su retirada de la selección española
elpais.description: El defensa del Atlético aclara que tomó la decisión antes de ser campeón del mundo

elpais.title: Muere a los 92 años Gloria Steinem, la gran impulsora del feminismo moderno
elpais.description: La escritora y periodista, referente de la revolución por los derechos de las mujeres, ha fallecido en su casa de Nueva York

elpais.title: Gloria Steinem: haz con tu vida lo que te apetezca
elpais.description: La contribución de esta icónica feminista fue práctica y cotidiana, aunque no siempre justamente valorada por las siguientes generaciones del feminismo

elpais.title: El futbolista del Real Madrid Asencio queda absuelto tras el perdón de las dos víctimas
elpais.description: Los excanteranos del equipo blanco Ferran Ruiz, Juan Rodríguez y Andrés García han aceptado una condena de un año de cárcel por pornografía infantil por el vídeo sexual que grabaron en 2023 en Gran Canaria

elpais.title: La Comunidad de Madrid fracasa en su intento de boicotear la reunión sobre la reforma del sistema de financiación
elpais.description: El quórum de la mitad de participantes que exige la normativa no peligra, dado que las autonomías del PP no secundan el plantón promovido por el Gobierno de Ayuso

nyt.title: U.S. Trade Gap Ballooned in July
nyt.description: The trade deficit bounced back up last month as spending on data centers to feed the A.I. boom drove up imports.

nyt.title: Mortgage Rates Hit 6.71%, Their Highest Level Since July 2025
nyt.description: Higher costs for home loans have put a squeeze on the housing market, adding pressure to consumers already struggling with elevated inflation.

nyt.title: Bessent Blames Ukraine for High Energy Prices
nyt.description: After meeting with Russia’s finance minister, the Treasury secretary said Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure were contributing to a global energy shock driven mainly by the U.S. war with Iran.

nyt.title: Dutch Central Bank Cuts Gold Reserves in U.S., Citing ‘Geopolitical Unrest’
nyt.description: The Netherlands moved some 90 tons of gold out of the Federal Reserve Bank in New York, the second European nation this year to announce it had decreased or eliminated U.S. gold holdings.

nyt.title: Volkswagen Plans to Cut 50,000 Jobs
nyt.description: Facing growing competition from China and rapidly advancing technology, the German auto giant said Thursday its board had approved a “comprehensive” overhaul.

nyt.title: Federal Prosecutors Charge ICE Agent With Lying About Minnesota Shooting
nyt.description: The charges are a rare instance of President Trump’s Justice Department accusing a federal agent of breaking the law while on the job.

nyt.title: Proposal for White House Visitor Screening Center Advances
nyt.description: A federal panel again paved the way for one of President Trump’s construction projects, even as it heard opposition to another proposal to fence in a park north of the White House.

nyt.title: Clancy’s Lawyer, Kevin Reddington, Became a Hero to Her Supporters
nyt.description: The themes present in Lindsay Clancy’s trial are not unfamiliar to Mr. Reddington, a veteran defense lawyer.

nyt.title: Gloria Steinem, Personification of the Feminist Movement, Dies at 92
nyt.description: She challenged sexist assumptions, helping women develop a sense of self-worth and gain a measure of equality at work, at home and in society at large.

nyt.title: Steinem’s Home, Where Feminism Flourished, Will Remain a Gathering Place
nyt.description: Following Ms. Steinem’s death on Wednesday, her foundation said her Upper East Side home would become a permanent space for organizing and activism.

nyt.title: Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham and Others Pay Tribute to Gloria Steinem
nyt.description: After Ms. Steinem’s death at 92, celebrities and politicians reflected on her decades of activism for women’s rights and equality.

nyt.title: Missouri Supreme Court Delivers Win for Democrats in Redistricting Case
nyt.description: The court said a map redrawn to benefit Republicans could not be used in November. Voters will decide whether the new boundaries ever take effect.

nyt.title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Allow Mail Voting Limits
nyt.description: The justices have been asked to weigh in again on the Trump administration’s efforts to restrict mail voting — this time on whether the plans violate the Constitution.

nyt.title: Judge Suggests Trump Mail-In Voting Rules Could Cause ‘Major Disenfranchisement’
nyt.description: Judge Indira Talwani said the Postal Service appeared to be trying a haphazard “experiment” with a new rule that could result in valid ballots being tossed.

nyt.title: The Start-Up That Helps People Die
nyt.description: Medical aid in dying is now legal in New York. A team of clinical professionals decided to create a practice to help their clients die on their own terms.

nyt.title: Maria Bartiromo Is Out at Fox News
nyt.description: The host, who appeared on Fox Business and Fox News, had been with the network for more than 12 years.

nyt.title: What Did Jurassic Forests Sound Like? Like This.
nyt.description: Scientists spent over a decade reconstructing the calls of nine species of ancient insects to create the first accurate Jurassic soundscape.

nyt.title: Tesla Begins Offering Rides in a Car Without a Steering Wheel
nyt.description: The new Cybercab embodies Elon Musk’s vision of cars that drive themselves, but it is not clear when the vehicle will be widely available.

npr.title: Nepali community in Texas grieves and prays for healing after flash floods
npr.description: Nepalese groups in North Texas, which has one of the largest communities of people from Nepal in the U.S., continue to grieve the loss of hundreds of people after the devastating floods in August.

npr.title: Dems demand DHS fund election security. And, journalist Gloria Steinem has died
npr.description: Two Democrats are demanding that Homeland Security officials fund election security ahead of the midterms. And, trail-blazing journalist Gloria Steinem has died.

npr.title: Families of the missing in Nepal's flash floods perform symbolic cremations
npr.description: Eight days after Nepal's flash floods, families who can't find loved ones perform symbolic cremations.

npr.title: China's Xi visits Egypt for the first time in a decade
npr.description: Xi Jinping's visit to Egypt for the first time in a decade, and during the Iran war, comes as U.S. allies broaden their security ties.

npr.title: Critics question legality of Venezuela oil deals
npr.description: Chevron's $7 billion Venezuela bet deepens U.S. ties to the country's oil industry. Critics say the deal poses risks to democracy and could fuel discontent over Washington's embrace of the government.

npr.title: U.S.-Israel relations are on the rocks ahead of elections
npr.description: Relations between the Trump administration and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have turned rocky since Trump called a truce with Iran. Trump seeks progress in Gaza, but Netanyahu is taking a defiant stance ahead of an election.

npr.title: Xi visits Egypt as China seeks deeper influence across the Mideast
npr.description: China's President Xi Jinping visits Egypt this week for the first time in a decade. The trip illustrates China's growing ambitions at a time when U.S. influence has been weakened by its war in Iran.

npr.title: Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and wife seek to end drug charges case on immunity grounds
npr.description: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife have asked a judge to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment against them on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country

npr.title: A jury in Malta acquits a businessman in the killing of reporter Daphne Caruana Galizia
npr.description: Investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia had written extensively about suspected corruption in political and business circles in Malta. She was killed by a car bomb in 2017, at age 53.

npr.title: Iran fires on its Gulf neighbors, retaliating for U.S. strikes after a monthlong lull
npr.description: The six-month war has led to a spike in oil prices, roiled the global economy and posed increasing political problems for President Trump's Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.

republika.title: Strage in famiglia a Pietralata, gli esami sulla pistola: “Hanno sparato entrambi i genitori”
republika.description: Le autopsie sui genitori di Bianca, la bambina di 5 anni uccisa nella villetta alla periferia Est di Roma, confermano tre colpi di pistola. Resta da chiarire la sequenza delle morti. Al vaglio degli investigatori anche i viaggi in Messico e i pagamenti per le cure della figlia

republika.title: Le pagelle dei look: da Orlando Bloom a Vittoria Ceretti e Kendall Jenner. E Malcovich in gorgiera
republika.description: Secondo red carpet per la Mostra del Cinema di Venezia, tutti gli outfit in passerella

republika.title: Natalia Paragoni sbarca al Lido con la testa rasata dopo la diagnosi del linfoma di Hodgkin
republika.description: L’influencer e modella ha condiviso sui social la malattia che le è stata diagnosticata all’ottavo mese di gravidanza

republika.title: Geppi Cucciari lascia Un giorno da pecora: “Ragioni editoriali, mi mancherà tantissimo”
republika.description: Spiega la conduttrice: "Fino all’ultima stagione potevo andare in onda da Milano per conciliare con Splendida cornice, quest’anno la soluzione è stata ritenuta impraticabile”

republika.title: Us Open in diretta: Cobolli lotta e va avanto. Fuori Musetti e Bellucci. Darderi al terzo turno
republika.description: Sui quattro azzurri sul cemento di New York due eliminazioni dolorose e due qualificazioni

republika.title: La procura militare indaga su Vannacci dopo la denuncia del sindacato: “Forze armate nel partito”
republika.description: L’inchiesta arriva dopo la denuncia del sindacato dei militari: approfondimenti sulla posizione di appartenenti alle forze armate nel movimento del generale

republika.title: Barberino di Mugello, rapisce la ex compagna e la getta dal cavalcavia in A1. Poi si toglie la vita
republika.description: Sul caso sta indagando la polizia. Federico Vella si sarebbe buttato subito dopo aver ucciso Lorena Isceri nel primo pomeriggio di oggi, 3 settembre, dal Viadotto Lora

republika.title: Malkovich verso l’Oscar con Wilde horse nine. Il regista: “Oggi gli Usa non agiscono più nell’ombra”
republika.description: In concorso a Venezia 83 il film di Martin McDonagh, ambientato nel Cile del 1973 dove il presidente Allende sta per essere ucciso nel colpo di Stato organizzato dal generale di Pinochet. Molto applaudito dalla stampa

republika.title: Finale Ligure, uccide la moglie e il figlio 15enne e si toglie la vita: in una lettera i motivi
republika.description: I corpi di Paola Siri, Daniele Baruzzo e del figlio, sono stati scoperti all'interno dell'appartamento intorno alle 12:30

republika.title: Preferenze o collegi: il campo largo e la battaglia degli opposti sulla legge elettorale
republika.description: Cosa propone il centrosinistra. Gli emendamenti unitari, le idee diverse e la causa comune contro il Melonellum

republika.title: Ostia, uccide la madre soffocandola con un cuscino poi si lancia dal balcone
republika.description: La tragedia è avvenuta in via del Mare di Tasman. Giorgio Prelec, 54 anni, è stato trovato morto in strada: Adriana Furlani aveva 83 anni

republika.title: Munizioni fantasma comprate in Italia per l’Ucraina, si dimette il ministro della Difesa estone
republika.description: Pevkur si fa da parte. Un’indagine interna ha rivelato che i proiettili di un’azienda della Spezia non sono mai arrivati a Kiev. Il contratto vale 70 milioni

republika.title: Le mail di Ranucci a Lavitola con l’intervista sul carbon credit: “Poi mandami i dati sul corruttore”
republika.description: In uno scambio di comunicazioni che Repubblica ha potuto visionare, il giornalista invia in anteprima le dichiarazioni rilasciate al giornale zimbabwese The Standard e riceve l’approvazione del faccendiere con un’emoticon

republika.title: I droni jet, la nuova arma di Putin
republika.description: Costano molto meno dei missili cruise convenzionali, si costruiscono più in fretta, sono facili da usare e causano danni terribili. Presto dilagheranno in tutto il pianeta: è solo questione di tempo

republika.title: Report, la conduzione a Claudia Di Pasquale. Corsini: “I nomi li scelgo io, Piervincenzi resta”
republika.description: Il dirigente Rai dopo la rinuncia di Giulia Presutti alla conduzione del programma d’inchiesta di RaiTre

republika.title: L’Onu: “Il Pianeta è in grave pericolo. El Niño ha proporzioni gigantesche, durerà fino a febbraio”
republika.description: Danni già in atto dal Sudamerica all'Indonesia. Nel Pacifico in formazione, in contemporanea, tre pericolosi uragani. “Serve una mobilitazione su scala globale”

republika.title: Caldo, domani inizia una nuova ondata. Ecco quando finirà questa estate anomala
republika.description: Ancora una settimana di temperature fino a 6-8 gradi sopra la media e punte di 37. Poi l’anticiclone africano potrebbe finalmente cedere sotto la spinta dell’aria fresca nord-atlantica. Ma il cambio di stagione rischia di essere brusco, con temporali e nubifragi

phys-org.title: Built to last or break down: Ring size tunes biodegradable plastic lifetimes
phys-org.description: Biodegradable plastics should be tough enough for use yet able to break down at an appropriate rate afterward. Researchers at the University of Osaka show that changing the size of rings threaded onto a biodegradable polymer can tune both its toughness and enzymatic degradation, offering a way to design material lifetimes. The study is published in ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering.

phys-org.title: Satellites spot forest stress two years before bark beetle die-offs become apparent
phys-org.description: Satellite measurements detected declining photosynthetic activity in Western U.S. forests two years before bark beetle mortality appeared in aerial detection surveys, according to new University of Utah-led research.

phys-org.title: The Arctic melt season is a week longer now than it was in the 1980s, new research on sea ice trends shows
phys-org.description: Relatively few people have been to the Arctic, and even fewer have set foot in Antarctica. Most people rely on imagination and the media to visualize these landscapes and the ways they are changing.

phys-org.title: Microbes—dead or alive—can be early indicators of soil health under regenerative farming
phys-org.description: Researchers have demonstrated a series of biological tests that could serve as "proxies" for measuring how different regenerative agriculture practices could improve soil carbon—years before it would be possible to measure the carbon directly. The technique offers new insights into how effective various regenerative practices are at improving soil health.

phys-org.title: Even second graders can reason like scientists—if we ask them the right way
phys-org.description: When a child asks "Why does a blowfish puff up?" we often jump in with facts. But what if we paused and suggested that they ask instead, "How does a blowfish puff up?" It may seem like splitting hairs, but this small shift in phrasing could help reshape future generations' capacity for reasoning and critical thought in science and beyond.

phys-org.title: Nanoscale multiferroic materials open the path to efficient magnetic memory technology
phys-org.description: With the rapid spread of cloud computing, artificial intelligence and data centers, global energy consumption is rising to new heights. A promising way to reduce this burden is to develop memory devices that store information magnetically yet are written using electric fields. Magnetic memories are nonvolatile, meaning stored information is retained without a power supply.

phys-org.title: Predictive tools can confuse rare mutations with dangerous ones
phys-org.description: When a patient's DNA is read, it is compared with a reference version of the human genome. This allows geneticists and rare disease experts to look at a list of places where the patient's DNA differs. Most variations will be harmless and shared with millions of other people, but some can cause illness.

phys-org.title: Beyond the 'Great Divide': What we really know about political polarization
phys-org.description: Americans are deeply divided. At least that's what we've been told for years. But how divided are we really? A new review suggests the answer may depend on how researchers ask the question.

phys-org.title: Ig Nobel Prize winners reveal why babies smell better than teenagers
phys-org.description: Babies smell wonderful—at least to their parents. An international research team of Ilona Croy, Tomasz Frackowiak, Thomas Hummel and Agnieszka Sorokowska investigated why teenagers lose this special olfactory advantage and has now been awarded an Ig Nobel Prize for the research.

phys-org.title: Traces of nearly 4 million coins reveal how Rome achieved economic integration
phys-org.description: For centuries, the study of ancient history relied primarily on interpreting classical texts and examining inscriptions and archaeological remains at their sites of origin or in museums. In recent years, however, a little-known transformation has profoundly changed this landscape. The digitization of extensive archaeological collections, coupled with the development of quantitative methods that can integrate millions of scattered records, is ushering in a new era of historical research. phys-org.title: 'Green thumb' molecule helps leaf stalks grow in crowded conditions
phys-org.description: Potassium (K) is one of the three essential nutrients for plants. It plays a critical role in a wide range of processes, including cell growth, photosynthesis and regulation of water balance. Plants take up K from the soil and circulate it throughout their bodies via molecules called K+ channels. The function of one such K+ channel (called AKT5) in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana has remained a mystery, despite more than 30 years of study.

phys-org.title: A molecular brake that keeps muscle architecture in check
phys-org.description: Every movement we make, from blinking to sprinting, depends on the ability of muscle fibers to contract in a rapid and coordinated way. Achieving this precision requires an intricate internal membrane network known as the transverse tubule, or T-tubule, system. These narrow membrane invaginations carry electrical signals from the cell surface deep into the muscle fiber, where they trigger the release of calcium needed for contraction.

phys-org.title: How a plant's refusal to self-pollinate could help India grow more of its own cooking oil
phys-org.description: Most people assume plants reproduce through whatever pollen happens to land on them. This is not true. A collaborative research initiative involving the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) has mapped and functionally tested the genes that control a natural "self-rejection" system in two widely grown Indian oilseed crops, Brassica rapa (mustard) varieties toria and yellow sarson. phys-org.title: Hot subdwarfs come into focus as AI scans thousands of stars in Gaia data
phys-org.description: There are myriad ways of "being a star," and scientists spend years trying to uncover and understand them. One unusual type is the so-called hot subdwarf—small stars that burn mysteriously hot for their size. Scientists from the Faculty of Physics and the Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics at Vilnius University (VU) are working to explain this strange phenomenon and recently made important breakthroughs.

phys-org.title: Perseverance rover watches Earth vanish behind Martian moon
phys-org.description: Earth and the Martian moon Phobos dance together in a series of images recently acquired by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover. Earth appears as a point of light in the Martian sky, disappearing behind the crescent of Phobos, the larger of Mars' two moons.

phys-org.title: 'Power of disorder' tames CF₄, a semiconductor greenhouse gas that can persist for 50,000 years
phys-org.description: Among the gases used in semiconductor manufacturing, tetrafluoromethane (CF₄) is a greenhouse gas more than 6,000 times as potent as carbon dioxide.

phys-org.title: 'Empty nest' can trigger loneliness and loss in older parents, study finds
phys-org.description: Older parents can experience loneliness, emotional distress and a loss of purpose when their children leave home, according to a new pilot study by the University of Hertfordshire.

phys-org.title: Antarctic expedition reveals why Southern Ocean clouds remain one of climate science's greatest challenges
phys-org.description: The Southern Ocean plays a pivotal role in regulating Earth's climate, yet the clouds that blanket this remote region remain among the least understood features in atmospheric science. By controlling both incoming sunlight and outgoing heat, these clouds strongly influence Earth's energy balance.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

proj-syn.title: India’s Resilience Depends on Diversified Trade
proj-syn.description: India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump’s return to the White House in an attempt to ensure that no single bilateral rupture will cause catastrophic harm. It should continue to expand its trade ties, while being wary of any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-à-vis third countries.

proj-syn.title: Whipsaw Trade Policy Is Depressing Foreign Direct Investment
proj-syn.description: If a country opts for higher trade restrictions to promote its perceived domestic interests, a predictable policy is far superior to a volatile one. As new research shows, uncertainty causes unnecessary and large collateral damage to FDI inflows.

proj-syn.title: Why the Far Right’s War on Modern Architecture Matters
proj-syn.description: The Alternative for Germany’s fixation on architecture is more revealing than it may seem. Cultural policy is not only one area where the party can actually change conditions on the ground at the state level; it is also intimately tied to far-right forces’ exclusionary political agenda.

proj-syn.title: How Will the US-Iran War End?
proj-syn.description: The latest US effort to subdue Iran—an "economic D-Day" intended to cut off the Islamic Republic from the world economy—can’t succeed without the support of the country’s biggest trade partner. The only stable solution to the impasse in the Gulf is one that involves China and increases economic integration in the region.

proj-syn.title: Germany’s Political Firewall Is Crumbling
proj-syn.description: The upcoming election in Saxony-Anhalt could give the far-right Alternative für Deutschland control of a state government for the first time in Germany’s postwar history. Its rise offers a crucial lesson for democracies elsewhere: closing ranks against extremist parties is no substitute for effective governance.

proj-syn.title: The Swimmable City Test
proj-syn.description: In committing to provide a safe swimmable place within 15 minutes of every home by 2035, London Mayor Sadiq Khan has set a measurable, time-bound goal that cannot be met through a single program or line item on the budget. Instead, it requires a public mission capable of mobilizing all ministries and shaping markets.

proj-syn.title: The Tale of Economics
proj-syn.description: A new book tells the story of the economics discipline and its original purpose with a degree of verve and imaginativeness that puts dreary mainstream economists to shame. In the process, it gets at fundamental truths that major schools within the discipline have managed to obscure.

proj-syn.title: AI’s Market Path Will Get Bumpier
proj-syn.description: By enhancing the input that goes into so much of what we do—intelligence—AI’s potential to drive higher economic growth is enormous. But with fears of the technology's unintended consequences affecting the pace and depth of adoption, the promise of long-term gains must be set against more immediate risks.

proj-syn.title: American Götterdämmerung
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump and his Treasury secretary’s latest desperate threats confirm how much American power has waned on their watch. Far from compelling others to join their efforts to isolate Iran, they are hastening the transition to a post-American world order.

proj-syn.title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
proj-syn.description: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
proj-syn.description: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

proj-syn.title: Building Canada’s Post-American Economy
proj-syn.description: Canada’s dependence on the US market has become a strategic liability, leaving it vulnerable to President Donald Trump’s bullying. Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.

proj-syn.title: Trump and Xi Should Align on AI
proj-syn.description: When potential outcomes are systemic and irreversible, preparation must precede certainty. This is the logic behind insurance, as well as every pandemic plan and arms-control treaty ever created, and it must be the principle that guides our approach to AI—beginning at the upcoming US-China summit.

proj-syn.title: The Quiet Revolution in Services
proj-syn.description: While economists debate whether industrialization can still play its traditional growth-promoting role in the current global and technological context, services have unexpectedly become an engine for economic development around the world. For developing and developed economies alike, the timing could not be better.

proj-syn.title: AI Addicts Won’t Make Better Workers
proj-syn.description: Economists widely agree that AI will boost labor productivity. But this view does not account for the possibility that hyperscalers will go all out to get people hooked on LLMs, because the narrower applications for which these tools are actually useful do not justify the massive investments made so far.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Crime Tax
proj-syn.description: Even excluding lives lost, communities displaced, and families ravaged, the economic costs of organized crime in the region produce a bleak picture, shaving 0.5–2 percentage points off annual GDP growth in the most affected countries. That, too, represents a hefty human toll.

proj-syn.title: Are The Walls Closing in on Bessent?
proj-syn.description: Far from suggesting financial Armageddon, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s futile efforts to keep a lid on Treasury yields suggest that, once again, the dollar is America’s currency, but everyone else’s problem. But while investors have few alternatives, the bond-salesman-in-chief cannot be complacent.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Reviving Chinese Marxist Economics
proj-syn.description: As recently as two years ago, most Chinese economists paid only lip service to Marxism and assigned Western textbooks to their students. The advent of AI has changed that, because the technology—open source and available to the smallest manufacturer for a pittance—promises to avoid the “rent trap” common to capitalist economies.
